summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 (CentOS Stream 10) as a 3-member MariaDB 10.11.18 Galera cluster with multi-master write availability and automatic resynchronization, then performed the mandatory sequential restart/recovery protocol on all three nodes.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera, rsync, mariadb-backup on all three nodes (EPEL enabled; AppStream already carried the packages)
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts and opened firewalld ports 3306, 4444, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568 on all nodes
Set SELinux booleans mysql_connect_any and daemons_enable_cluster_mode on all nodes, fixing an AVC denial that blocked mariadb-backup from connecting to the local mysqld socket during SST

Disabled the packaged default /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf (it forced wsrep_on=0 and silently overrode our config due to alphabetical load order) and wrote a custom 60-galera.cnf per node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and wsrep_sst_method=mariabackup
Generated sstuser and root credentials on-node via openssl rand, propagated only through secret_env, never in command text or this report
Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, created the sstuser grant, then sequentially started node2 and node3 which joined via mariabackup SST/IST
Verified multi-master replication by writing distinct rows from each of the three nodes and confirming identical result sets on all three
Demonstrated availability: stopped node3, wrote through node1 and node2 while cluster stayed Primary at size 2, confirming writes survive a member outage

Demonstrated automatic resync: restarted node3 and confirmed it automatically caught up via IST to cluster size 3 / Synced / Primary with the rows written during its outage present, with no manual resync action taken

Ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/cluster health on all nodes, rebooted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time, quorum preserved throughout since Galera keeps 2/3 majority), polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and uptime on each, and confirmed each rejoined the cluster (size 3, Synced, Primary) with correct data after mariadb auto-started on boot

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster formed, writes visible from any member
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped (wsrep_cluster_size=1, Synced, Primary), node2 and node3 joined via SST to reach size 3; a row inserted separately on each node appears identically on all three nodes' SELECT results

evidence.requirement: SELinux/firewall fix required for SST to function at all (mariadb-backup connectto AVC denial)
evidence.summary: AVC denial captured via kernel audit log, resolved with the vendor-provided daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean on all nodes, after which SST succeeded

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is down
evidence.summary: node3 stopped; wsrep_cluster_size dropped to 2 with cluster_status still Primary; writes via node1 and node2 succeeded and replicated between the two remaining members

node3 restarted and, without manual intervention, rejoined via IST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and its SELECT shows the rows written while it was down
A row written on node1 after all restarts appears with identical COUNT(*)=6 on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart: boot_id d4784d1b, uptime start 07:02:49, cluster size 3/Synced. Reboot acknowledged then connection reset (disconnect proof). Post-restart: boot_id changed to c170800a, uptime start moved to 07:09:21, mariadb active and rejoined cluster (size 3, Synced, Primary) with correct row count

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart: boot_id 984a7d52, uptime start 07:02:49, cluster size 3/Synced. Reboot acknowledged then connection reset. Post-restart: boot_id changed to bfb95995, uptime start moved to 07:09:40, mariadb active and rejoined cluster (size 3, Synced, Primary) with correct row count
